problem: The release walkthrough uses 2.0.0 throughout (branch, prepare, commit, PR). v2.0.0 and v2.1.0 are already tagged, and `prepare` refuses a version that is already released or not newer than the latest, so the block fails as written.
replacement: Use a placeholder throughout the block: `release/vX.Y.Z`, `changelog.py prepare X.Y.Z`, `chore(release): vX.Y.Z`, with a line saying X.Y.Z must be newer than the latest tag.
subject: python scripts/changelog.py prepare 2.0.0

evidence.docstring: Deleting the fragment files is the caller's job, after the result is written.

problem: Says `changelog.py prepare` creates a commit. It only rewrites CHANGELOG.md (and the fragments/ledgers); the person commits, as step 2's own block shows (`git commit -m "chore(release): vX.Y.Z"`).
replacement: the subject of the commit you make after `changelog.py prepare`
route_reason: Which commands make a commit isn't something an extractor reads, and the CLI isn't an MCP tool an executed example can run.
subject: the subject of the commit `changelog.py prepare` creates

problem: The paragraph hedges on how GitHub's merge queue builds the squash subject ('community reports say… other reports say…') and asks for a check 'until a release has gone through the queue'. One has: v2.1.0 merged through the queue as `chore(release): v2.1.0 (#821)`, after #649. The external behaviour still needs checking, but the open question is answered by the repo's own history.
replacement: Replace the hedging with the record: "v2.1.0 (#821) was the first release through the queue; its squash subject was the PR title plus ` (#N)`, which `tag-release.yml` accepts." Drop the 'Until a release has gone through the queue' check, keeping only 'if the subject doesn't start with chore(release): vX.Y.Z, nothing is tagged'.
subject: Until a release has gone through the queue

problem: The section never says when to use it. Run after a normal release merge, a hand-pushed tag races `tag-release.yml`, and the page's own merge-queue paragraph says to fix forward 'rather than tagging by hand'.
replacement: Start the section with its precondition: "Only when `tag-release.yml` did not tag a merged release PR (check `git tag -l vX.Y.Z`); never alongside it." and use vX.Y.Z in the example.
subject: Pushing a tag by hand still runs `release.yml` directly

problem: PENDING-CONFIG: the sample `ls dist/` output names the wheel after the project's old name. pyproject.toml's `[project] name` is `pyeye-mcp`, so `uv build` writes `pyeye_mcp-<version>-py3-none-any.whl`.
replacement: pyeye_mcp-X.Y.Z-py3-none-any.whl (and `# At tag vX.Y.Z` / `# Output: X.Y.Z` above it)
subject: python_code_intelligence_mcp-0.3.0-py3-none-any.whl
